text:
Peyton Krebs finally scored on Nov. 4 against Ottawa, the kind of headline (CBS Sports: "Finally lights lamp") that tells you how long the wait felt. He still has just one goal, but 9 points in 16 games is a better line than his ice time suggests: 2.44 points per 60 minutes, above the league's typical forward.

We'd be careful, though. Buffalo has scored about 5.9 more goals than its chances deserve with Krebs on the ice, and the Sabres take only 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he plays at five on five, more than five points worse than without him. His three-assist night in the 7-6 win in Anaheim did a lot of lifting.

What he brings is real enough: top-end speed in the 84th percentile, more passer than finisher. He is one assist from 100 for his career. Our numbers project about 41 points by April, which would be a perfectly useful season for a third-line center. Just don't expect the on-ice shooting to stay this kind.
headline: Nine points, one goal, and some luck
